theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.equations: a=dt/(2*tau+dt); b=(2*tau-dt)/(2*tau+dt); lag_n=a*(u_n+u_(n-1))+b*lag_(n-1); rate_n=clip(lag_n, rate_(n-1)-r*dt, rate_(n-1)+r*dt); output=clip(rate_n,low,high); Passive: I_w*wheel_dot=T_drive-(wind_damping+bearing_damping)*wheel; Passive: I_h*hinge_ddot+hinge_damping*hinge_dot+(hinge_stiffness+q*H_delta)*hinge=-I_w*wheel*body_roll_rate

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.equations: a=dt/(2*tau+dt); b=(2*tau-dt)/(2*tau+dt); lag_n=a*(u_n+u_(n-1))+b*lag_(n-1); rate_n=clip(lag_n, rate_(n-1)-r*dt, rate_(n-1)+r*dt); output=clip(rate_n,low,high); Passive: I_w*wheel_dot=T_drive-(wind_damping+bearing_damping)*wheel; Passive: I_h*hinge_ddot+hinge_damping*hinge_dot+(hinge_stiffness+q*H_delta)*hinge=-I_w*wheel*body_roll_rate

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.equations: a=dt/(2*tau+dt); b=(2*tau-dt)/(2*tau+dt); lag_n=a*(u_n+u_(n-1))+b*lag_(n-1); rate_n=clip(lag_n, rate_(n-1)-r*dt, rate_(n-1)+r*dt); output=clip(rate_n,low,high); Passive: I_w*wheel_dot=T_drive-(wind_damping+bearing_damping)*wheel; Passive: I_h*hinge_ddot+hinge_damping*hinge_dot+(hinge_stiffness+q*H_delta)*hinge=-I_w*wheel*body_roll_rate

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.equations: a=dt/(2*tau+dt); b=(2*tau-dt)/(2*tau+dt); lag_n=a*(u_n+u_(n-1))+b*lag_(n-1); rate_n=clip(lag_n, rate_(n-1)-r*dt, rate_(n-1)+r*dt); output=clip(rate_n,low,high); Passive: I_w*wheel_dot=T_drive-(wind_damping+bearing_damping)*wheel; Passive: I_h*hinge_ddot+hinge_damping*hinge_dot+(hinge_stiffness+q*H_delta)*hinge=-I_w*wheel*body_roll_rate

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.equations: a=dt/(2*tau+dt); b=(2*tau-dt)/(2*tau+dt); lag_n=a*(u_n+u_(n-1))+b*lag_(n-1); rate_n=clip(lag_n, rate_(n-1)-r*dt, rate_(n-1)+r*dt); output=clip(rate_n,low,high); Passive: I_w*wheel_dot=T_drive-(wind_damping+bearing_damping)*wheel; Passive: I_h*hinge_ddot+hinge_damping*hinge_dot+(hinge_stiffness+q*H_delta)*hinge=-I_w*wheel*body_roll_rate

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.

theory.limits: Upstream initialization bypasses lag/rate on the first uninitialized sample; comparisons warm at zero before measured command steps. Rate/stops make continuous LTI comparisons valid only in their inactive domain. Passive reduced roll/hinge model is not a calibrated six-axis gyro assembly; no fake FGActuator demand/malfunction properties are supplied.
theory.delta: Active fins and passive rollerons are different physical roles despite one shared selected actuator descriptor. Actual XML kind1 driven fins require FGActuator ports; kind2 passive patches require wheel/hinge/identity/bounds and retain unavailable driven-demand/malfunction fields.
theory.state: Native FGActuator distinct previous lag input/output and previous rate-limited output; malfunction flags, delay/history where authored. R77M exposes lag_filter separately to predict its real state. Passive gyro wheel speed/hinge angle/rate belong to PassiveRolleronV1, not FGActuator.
theory.io: Driven: physical command radians and native lag/rate/asymmetric limits -> actual radians. Passive: actual airspeed/density/body rates/current CG and source mechanical parameters -> wheel/hinge states and reaction force/torque/energy. No command or target input to passive dynamics.
theory.discretization: Initialized driven lag uses trapezoidal/Tustin integration; rate limit precedes hard stops and its internal history must not be replaced by clipped output. Native failure order is fail-zero, hardover, stuck branch, lag/rate/deadband/hysteresis/bias/delay, then clip. Passive RK4 uses bounded physical substeps, stage-wise hinge stop/rate constraints, explicit dissipative/gyro work ledgers.
theory.uncertainty: Native card lag/rate records preserve uncertainty. Passive mechanical inputs carry their separate declared relative-input uncertainty (generic engineering estimates), so one driven-lag reference does not establish passive hardware calibration.
